terms: §1: construct validity is what a score measures; metric validity is whether its metric measures that target; criterion validity is whether it tracks held-out behavior.

§3.2: all scores are oriented so that higher is safer. R-Judge specificity is the fraction of benign traces correctly identified as benign. Balanced accuracy averages performance on benign and unsafe traces. InjecAgent robustness = 1 − attack success. AgentHarm safety = 1 − harmful compliance.
§3.3: the capability composite is the mean of the standardized MMLU (500-item zero-shot subset) and GPQA-Diamond (198 items, chain-of-thought) anchors, both measured under one protocol.
§3.3: partial Spearman correlations control for the capability composite by residualizing midranks on it and re-ranking the residuals (A.5).

§3.3: the three held-out criteria are τ²-bench retail task success (40 tasks); misalignment safety (avoiding blackmail or leaking in a fictional agent scenario, 100 decisions per model); and jailbreak safety (1 − StrongREJECT harmful compliance on 50 prompts, averaged over three templates).

§3.3: three controls were pre-specified. Positive: capability anchors load ≥0.6 on the first factor. Negative: a column-permuted matrix falls within the parallel-analysis null. Convergent: InjecAgent and AgentDojo correlate highly.
§3.3: the decision rule allows interpreting the factor structure only if first-factor variance is ≥40% or controlling capability reduces the median partial |ρ| by ≥0.15, and the controls pass.
§4.1 Observation 1: under F1, a constant always-positive policy on base rate π scores 2π/(1+π), because F1 gives no credit for true negatives.
